proposals.name: The Gravoska Kingdom
proposals.entry:
The Gravoska Kingdom is one of the great powers of the 99 War. It occupies a vast northern country of mountains, conifer forests, glacial valleys, deep fjords and cold seas.

Its military technology is generally simpler than that of Veyr, but Gravoska excels at producing rugged weapons, ammunition, armor, ships and enormous artillery pieces that can be maintained far from sophisticated workshops.

The kingdom’s famous longboat fleets operate on rivers, coasts and open seas, while its Great Bombards threaten targets at extraordinary distances. Its present ruler is Kavra Morn, who bears the ancient title First Witness.

Government

The monarch possesses enormous authority but does not theoretically create law. Gravosk law precedes the crown. The First Witness is expected to interpret, defend and obey it. A ruler can therefore be publicly told: “You are wrong.” There are formal procedures for doing exactly that.

The Muster

Nearly every adult owes a period of national service. The Muster does not necessarily mean infantry service. Foresters, cooks, artillery workers, armorers, healers, sailors, teamsters, shipwrights, road crews and quartermasters all fulfill military obligations. Consequently the kingdom does not need to create an army when war begins. Much of the population already knows where to report.

The Drusha Alliance

The kingdom’s closest foreign allies are the Drusha, engineer-warlocks whose friendship with the Gravosk began during the Winter of 176. Among the most visible products of that alliance are Lumber Matons, which the Drusha manufacture from Gravosk timber and return aboard Gravosk ships.

Great Works

The greatest surviving engineering achievement of pre-war Gravoska is the Ship-Stair of Keld, which allows longboats to cross an otherwise impassable mountain watershed.

posts.name: Gamemaster Only
posts.entry:
Several old Gravosk bombard fortifications face inward toward Gravoska rather than toward any historical enemy. Their ammunition vaults were maintained long after the reason for their construction was supposedly forgotten.

Deep below the royal seat lies an unfinished weapon described in ancient work orders only as “The Answer.”
